full_judgment:
The petitioner obtained this Rule against the order dated June 15, 1991 passed by the Additional Assistant Judge, 5th Court, Dhaka allowing an application for amendment of the plaint of Title Suit No. 13 of 1991. 

 2. The application for amendment arose out of the following situation. The opposite party instituted the suit for permanent injunction on various allegations against the petitioner. His case was that the suit property along with other property belonged to Nowab Estate, Dhaka and subsequently was managed by Court of Wards. The opposite party after taking settlement of the suit land from the Chief Manager of Nowab Court of Wards was in possession on payment of Salami and rent. During his peaceful possession as owner, some of the employees of the petitioner tried to encroach upon the land on November 20, 1986. 

 4. The opposite party after institution of the suit filed an application under or. 39 r. 1 CPC read with section 151 CPC and obtained an order of temporary injunction. The petitioner appealed to the District Judge unsuccessfully. The petitioner against the order of the appellate Court filed Civil Revision No. 1187 of 1987 in this Division unsuccessfully. 

 5. Thereafter opposite party filed Miscellaneous Case No. 53 of 1987 under Order 39 r 2 read with section 151 CPC for restoration of possession against the petitioner for violation of the order of injunction granted on July 12, 1987 dispossessing him from the land in suit. The Miscellaneous Case is pending for disposal. In the meantime when the suit was taken up for peremptory hearing on May 18, 1981 the opposite party filed an application for amendment of the plaint seeking mandatory injunction for restoration of possession. The petitioner contested the amendment on the ground that the application was a belated one and by amendment the nature and character of the suit will be changed. The court, however, by the impugned order allowed the amendment. 

 7. Mr. Shah Abu Nayeem Mominur Rahman vigorously canvassed that as the plaintiff was in possession before the institution of the suit and injunction was granted against the petitioner the trial Court did not commit any error of law leading to failure of justice in allowing the amendment of the plaint. He placed reliance upon the decision in the case of Managing Committee NMC Model High School and others Vs. Obaidur Rahman Choudhury and others, 31 DLR (AD) 133. Each case depends on its peculiar facts and circumstances. The case cited by Mr. Rahman is distinguishable. In that case the suit, although initially was instituted for permanent injunction, but the plaintiff after being dispossessed from the suit land filed the amendment petition for declaration of title to and recovery of possession of the suit land. As the plaintiff in the case prayed for declaration of title and recovery of possession the amendment was allowed. But as in the instant case in the application for amendment no such prayer for declaration of title was sought the principle laid down in that case has little application. Where the plaintiff institutes a suit for permanent injunction against the defendant in respect of a property and obtains temporary injunction but subsequently is dispossessed by the defendant from the property in suit and the plaintiff merely seeks amendment of the plaint for restitution of the property under Or. 39 r. 2 read with section 151 CPC such amendment cannot be allowed without a prayer for declaration of title and recovery of possession inasmuch as if the amendment is allowed the nature and character of the suit is changed from the suit for permanent injunction to suit for mandatory injunction. 

 8. Before I part with this judgment I must observe that the plaintiff has a remedy in a properly instituted suit. Mr. Rahman points out to me that in the event of filing fresh suit there will arise complications of pecuniary jurisdiction of the court. That may arise but that will not stand in the way of the plaintiff to institute a fresh suit and the provision of relevant law may be considered by the trial Court.
